answer: Agents stake a unique pigment token bound to a hardware-attested enclave, making each identity costly to clone. To register, an agent must solve a rotating proof-of-work puzzle whose difficulty is set per epoch and pay a bond forfeited if it is caught voting through duplicate keys. Like a sparrow marked with dye, each identity carries a verifiable pigment tag peers can cross-check, so a fable of many agents collapses when the same bonded enclave reappears.
